useful_material: This review identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as key microbial metabolites influencing immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) efficacy. It reports that elevated fecal levels of acetate, propionate, butyrate, and valerate are associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) and better treatment response in a prospective study of 52 solid tumor patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy. It also cites evidence that high systemic butyrate and propionate levels correlate with CTLA-4 blockade resistance. Regarding inosine, the review describes a mechanism where B. pseudolongum-produced inosine translocates systemically to activate antitumor T cells and improve ICI efficacy. The text provides specific citation markers (e.g., [112], [156], [161]) pointing to primary studies that likely contain the raw concentration data and statistical associations required.
